subject.title: WhatsApp: Add support for querying message reactions

question: Should WhatsApp reactions first be exposed as passive, access-controlled plugin events only, or should OpenClaw also commit to a generic historical `message reactions` query backed by retained reaction state?
rationale: The issue combines two materially different products—live observation and historical querying—with different privacy, storage, upgrade, and routing consequences; source evidence does not establish a current maintainer-approved contract.

options.title: Define passive hooks first
options.body: Add a non-agent-turn reaction event/hook contract with access controls and removals, then evaluate retained query support separately.

options.title: Commit to full query support
options.body: Specify durable reaction retention, lookup authority, privacy boundaries, and the generic WhatsApp reaction-query API before implementation.

options.title: Decline retained history
options.body: Support live passive events only and document that historical WhatsApp reaction lookup is not an OpenClaw contract.

recommendation.title: Define passive hooks first
recommendation.body: Add a non-agent-turn reaction event/hook contract with access controls and removals, then evaluate retained query support separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this contributor most directly to the current WhatsApp action and inbound implementation paths.
